snippet.title: The Exorcist: Believer Behind the scenes
snippet.description:
The Exorcist: Believer is a new – expensive – path for Blumhouse! Universal invested 400 million dollars into this production with two potential sequels to follow suit. Jason Blum says this is the riskiest movie of his career because every other Blumhouse movie doesn’t go past the 10 million dollar mark. The bar is high! Apparently, though, they’re trying to follow in the footsteps of the Halloween sequel that was released in 2018, but in a bit of a different way. With Halloween, there’s so much to reference over the past thirty years, but with The Exorcist, it’s going to be a bit of a fresh take with subtle nods to the original. One thing that’s keeping this movie grounded in the 1973 story is the return of Ellen Burstyn’s iconic character Chris MacNeil. She was super excited to step back into the shoes of a character she invented fifty years ago and imagine all of the things that she might’ve gone through over all that time. Wild! There are so many creepy things about this movie – especially the girls! Lydia Jewett and Olivia Marcum really got into character in ways that extend far beyond the make up they were wearing. Some lines they delivered sent chills up everyone’s spine on set. They had to adjust their acting accordingly depending on just how possessed they were and it definitely shows! The Exoricst: Believer is going to be a wild ride for any horror fan and lover of the 1973 classic!

snippet.description:

The movie looks like it is going to incorporate the first four games, which include a prequel to the story. For those of you who don’t know the premise, you start out by just playing night watch security at a pizzeria. It seems pretty simple, except the animatronics come to life at night to brutally end whoever they come across. I’m not sure what the night watch security salary is, but I’m positive it’s not nearly enough for that. It was also founded by William Afton who owns a robotics company… he is, unfortunately, also a murderer. He was trying to lure five children in with the family-friendly appeal only to brutally end their lives and shove them into the animatronic characters of the pizzeria. There is also the deep lore about Scott Cawthon himself. He didn’t get his start in horror, he started out making Christian video games and then transitioning into the family friend genre, before getting so many negative reviews on the way his characters look, that it turned into Five Nights At Freddy’s. There is also the exciting fact that we’re definitely going to be getting into the bite of ‘83. It’s been confirmed that we do see Mike as a kind in the movie, and the only time we see Young Mike in the game is for that moment. I’m getting into all of this and more! snippet.title: Dumb Money : Cast Experience
snippet.description:
Dumb Money brings us an incredible true story about Game Stop and the power that regular people hold when it comes to determining value. The plot of this movie took place during the Pandemic – that’s also when the idea to make it into a movie was born as well. This was one of the fastest greenlit ideas in Hollywood history. Coming up with the idea for the movie, getting their hands on the intellectual property, and getting everyone on board to make it only took three days. The way it was shot was also super interesting – the actors were pretty much by themselves on set for an entire week. It felt like everyone was the star of their own little movie and even tricked the actors into thinking that everything was happening simultaneously. There was also a ton of inspiration from the real people that the actors were able to pull from. Paul Dano honed in on how authentic and honest Keith Gill was in his portrayal of his character, and Shailene Woodley finds this role to be extremely ironic because she’s studied so much about finance and investing and can’t comprehend any of it in her real life. There’s also so much truth behind the writing of this movie – there are many things that were taken straight from real life and put right into the script. For example, Seth Rogen’s character actually did buy two mansions side by side in Miami and tear one down to make a tennis court for his family. Can you imagine? Maybe Dumb Money can help us all out!

snippet.title: Why Bonnie Wright Was Upset About her Screen Time in the Harry Potter Series
snippet.description:
Harry Potter is one of the most popular book series out there, and while it was a tall order to adapt such a beloved series into a film franchise, the folks involved with the Harry Potter movies outdid themselves and made a series that’s just as beloved as its source material. Still, living up to the books was certainly a challenge when it came to making these movies. 

Bonnie Wright played the role of Ginny Weasley, and she’s recently called out Ginny’s screen time and how she struggled to feel that she was doing her character justice when Ginny had so much more room to grow in the books than she did in the movies. Still, despite how differently Ginny’s character was able to develop in the books, she still went in a different direction than Wright originally anticipated. Wright has been very open about her experience working on the films, and it’s clear just how intimidating it was taking on a role with such a massive fanbase and so much love from folks who knew her from the books. 
Wright may not have always been entirely pleased with what she was able to do as Ginny Weasley in the films, but that didn’t stop her from turning an iconic novel character into an iconic on-screen character, and it’s clear that Wright was able to overcome her concerns and give an incredible performance.

snippet.title: The Meg 2 : Things You Missed
snippet.description:
The Meg 2 is filled with subtle Easter eggs paying homage to many iconic horror movies, but most obviously, Jaws. The fresh take it has on the monster movie genre is sure to keep you on your toes! The film ends with a major foreshadowing of a future installment where Meiying could possibly wind up pregnant many years in the future as she and the Meg’s stories continue to intertwine. Jason Statham did most of his own stunt work in the movie, including the dangerous jet ski scene, which made the director and crew worried for his safety. Every shot of him upside down was actually him being flipped and turned while strapped to a hand drill! The film does not fail to pay homage to its predecessor, creating cinematic shots that take the audience back to the Jaws franchise, such as the open-mouth shot of the swimmers inside the Meg’s mouth, or the helicopter blade impalement scene. There is also a small dog named Pippin who makes a return in each installment, reminiscent of the dog that disappears in Jaws 2 before a shark attack. The Meg 2 even has a reference to the hilarious glass smash shot from Jaws 3D, where Wu Jing's Jiuming attempts to train the Meg with a clicker, causing it to charge forward almost into a window. Luckily, he was pulled up in the nick of time! Overall, The Meg 2 is a perfect blend of classic Jaws energy and modern-day suspense, making it a must-see for horror film enthusiasts.

snippet.title: The Last Voyage of the Demeter Cast Experience
snippet.description:
“The Voyage of the Demeter” is based on one chapter of Bram Stoker’s “Dracula” and it delivers quite the terrifying punch – not only for the audience but for the cast and crew as well! One thing they wanted in this movie was for everything to be as practical as they could have it. That included the ship, the rain, and of course, Dracula himself. Javier Botet was the actor inside the horrifying Dracula suit and his castmates could barely look at him throughout filming. He was so into character that every movement he did with his body just shot chills down everyone’s spine. It also didn’t help that the ship was absolutely massive and they built it as one huge set piece to create a sense of fear that you never knew exactly which corner he could be lurking around. This film is also backed by huge names like Steven Spielberg, so the pressure was on for everyone to deliver their best performance! Not only did everyone have to get a handle on their fear, but they had to get a handle on knot-tying as well! Everyone had to go through a sailing boot camp before filming started because they were going to essentially be manning a real ship through a storm. Even though the environment was often frightening, a lot of the actors described it as a way for them to be childlike because everything felt so incredibly real, they were able to get lost in the imaginary world – even if that world has a scary, demonic Dracula right in the center.

snippet.title: Gran Turismo Behind the scenes
snippet.description:
Gran Turismo takes the concept of 'based on a true story' to an unprecedented level by bringing the remarkable tale of racecar driver Jann Mardenborough to life through a dynamic cinematic experience. The film showcases Mardenborough's journey with heart-pounding scenes of exotic cars reaching speeds of 200 miles per hour, innovative camera angles that immerse the audience, and Mardenborough stunt driving with authenticity. The film's production team faced the challenge of capturing the intense speeds on camera, with cars racing at 140 to 200 miles per hour. They utilized a detachable camera called "Rialto," allowing versatile placement and authentic perspectives both inside and outside the cars. This technology enabled a genuine portrayal of speed and action. Innovative photography techniques contributed to the immersive experience, creating a fresh and visceral portrayal of speed. The film's focus on capturing the essence of velocity led to an intentional elimination of extraneous elements in the frames. Low camera angles and close proximity to the track provided a new level of engagement for viewers, enhancing the sense of racing intensity. The movie showcases iconic race tracks around the world, featuring a diverse range of exotic cars from Lamborghinis to McLarens. Raw and intense shots were achieved using unstabilized cameras attached to the exteriors of the cars, particularly in challenging conditions like night and rain. The rigorous training that goes into race car driving is highlighted, with actor Archie Madekwe undergoing intense physical preparation to authentically portray a driver. His dedication to realism led to instances of discomfort, but he committed to delivering genuine performances inside and outside of the race car.

snippet.title: Disney's Elemental - Behind the voices
snippet.description:
No team makes hit after hit quite the way Disney and Pixar do. This year’s new film, Elemental, is certainly no exception. This movie was an instant classic, and as is true with so many Disney and Pixar films, the amazingly talented cast of voice actors had a lot to do with how much audiences fell in love with these characters. 

So, how did this cast come together, and what made them so good at bringing their characters to life? Elemental’s director, Peter Sohn, clearly set out to build a cast that could relate particularly well to their characters. As a result, the film has folks behind it who really knew how to get into each other’s heads. Of course, there are amazing comedic actors like Catherine O’Hara, Wendi McLendon-Covey, and Joe Pera, who managed to add some new faces to their lists of iconic roles. But, other actors’ relationships with their characters ran especially deep. Mamoudou Athie played Wade Ripple, and since he was getting his U.S. citizenship while filming, his character’s story of being an immigrant hit especially close to home. Shila Ommi and Ronnie Del Carmen, who played Cinder and Bernie Lumen also had special ties to their immigrant characters. Leah Lewis played Ember Lumen, and she really related to her character’s spicy personality and fierce loyalty and love of family.

Learning more about this amazing group of voice actors makes this already enjoyable movie even more fun.

snippet.title: Oppenheimer: Behind the Scenes and Filming Secrets!
snippet.description:
Oppenheimer, the historical film by Christopher Nolan, promises to be an intense and groundbreaking production. The cast's experience when shooting this film is unlike any other. Behind the scenes there is a huge focus on authenticity – the film utilizes practical effects instead of CGI, even shooting off actual explosives on set. Cillian Murphy, who portrays J. Robert Oppenheimer, dove deep into the character, collaborating closely with Christopher Nolan to ensure the most accurate portrayal possible. Matt Damon, playing Leslie Groves, immersed himself in historical research to capture the essence of his character, who played a pivotal role in the creation of the nuclear bomb that was used to end World War 2. The nuke scene, shot with astonishing realism, required the use of new technologies and left a lasting impression on the cast and crew. They shot that scene at the very end because they knew they were going to have to be extremely innovative when it came to utilizing technology to get it done. Nolan's dedication to practical effects extends throughout the movie, with meticulous attention given to real sets and locations. The film's black-and-white shots were designed specifically for IMAX, showcasing the team's innovative approach to cinematography. Another unique aspect of the film is its first-person narrative style that was written into the script, allowing viewers and readers to experience Oppenheimer's journey intimately. Christopher Nolan has elevated "Oppenheimer" through his commitment to character development, lifelike sets, and remarkable attention to detail.

snippet.title: How the Cast of Barbie Turned Plastic
snippet.description:
The Barbie movie was filled with tons of fun and many interesting behind-the-scenes moments. Margot Robbie hosted a Barbie sleepover for the cast – not a single Ken allowed – where they hung out, shared beds, and ordered room service. There was a running joke about how America Ferrera couldn’t remember meeting any of her co-stars prior to shooting the film. The movie also highlighted Ryan Gosling’s incredible comedic talent, often causing Margot Robbie to break character with her laughter. Issa Rae had to learn a dance sequence in under 24 hours while the rest of the cast had already been working on it for days. Margot Robbie also got to have one of her childhood fantasies fulfilled when she asked Greta Gerwig if she could have a real-life Barbie dream house with a slide that goes from her bedroom all the way down to the pool. Greta said no problem on that one. The movie addresses the evolution of Barbie, which was a big reason why America Farrera even ended up joining the cast because it not only highlights the positives of Barbie’s effect on society but the negatives as well. Margot Robbie was invested in the project for years, but never saw herself as being the one to actually play the role of Barbie – not for many years down the line, anyway. Overall, the stellar combination of Margot Robbie and Greta Gerwig proved to be a major success in bringing the iconic character of Barbie into the real world.

snippet.title: Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny - Behind the Scenes
snippet.description:
You can clearly tell that the cast of Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny had a lot of fun working on this movie! This sequel from the Walt Disney Company brings back Harrison Ford, well known for his work in the Star Wars franchise and Blade Runner, in the titular role of Indiana Jones, though this time with a bit of a twist: he’s a much older man now! But that being said, we will get to see a younger version of the character in flashbacks, thanks to the help of AI-assisted visual effects technology pulling Indiana Jones expressions from the Lucasfilm library. Phoebe Waller-Bridge is known for her work on Fleabag and Solo: A Stars Wars Story, but here she stars as Indy's goddaughter, Helena Shaw. Phoebe Waller-Bridge was a huge fan of the way that her co-star Antonio Banderas would do the Puss in Boots impression whenever you asked, and considering he’s become synonymous with the role that started out in Dreamworks’ Shrek, we imagine that it was pretty great! Mads Mikkelsen has played a multitude of villains, between his role on the Harry Potter franchise film Fantastic Beasts: the Secrets of Dumbledore and the Marvel Cinematic Universe film Doctor Strange, but here he portrays the villainous Jürgen Voller, which is perfect for his skill set! Toby Jones is best known for his work on The Hunger Games and Captain America: the First Avenger, but plays Basil Shaw in this movie. John Williams returns with an all-new score.

snippet.title: The Bear Behind The Scenes
snippet.description:
Let’s delve behind the scenes of The Bear! It’s a critically acclaimed show with a dedicated cast and crew bringing it to life. Season two boasted an impressive lineup of guest stars included, but not limited to, Sarah Paulson, Jamie Lee Curtis, and Molly Gordon. Jeremy Allen White, who portrays the show’s protagonist, Carmy, went to great lengths to prepare for his role. He immersed himself in real kitchens to truly understand the back-of-house world his character was so engulfed by. Due to his lack of experience, he found himself constantly apologizing to the kitchen staff he was learning from. Jeremy and his co-star, Ayo Edebiri were enrolled in a two week crash course at the Institute of Culinary Education in Pasadena where they learned as much as they could about the craft – including how to use knives safely and effectively. Something really cool about the set is that it was built completely on a sound stage, but everything actually works – the fire, the plumbing – it’s all real! The cast would often get in trouble in between takes for eating the food that was being prepared for the show – yes, the food was all real and delicious. The show also resonated strongly with the restaurant industry, causing everyone who ran into Jeremy to refer to him only as “chef.” It resonated so strongly – some described their time in the kitchen as traumatizing – leading them to have a really difficult time actually watching and finishing the show.

snippet.title: Every Ben Affleck Movie That Has Grossed Over $100 Million At The Box Office
snippet.description:
Most of us know that Ben Affleck is a man of many, many talents. He’s likely best known for his varied and long acting career, but he’s also an acclaimed, Academy Award-winning director and writer. In fact, he was the youngest person to ever win the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay at only 25 years old. Now, at just 50 years old, when plenty of folks in show business are just getting started, he already has 131 award nominations and 54 wins under his belt for many different kinds of work. Besides the acclaim he’s received, Affleck has been a part of films that have earned lots and lots of money. While most people only dream of making a movie that grosses over $100 million at the box office, Affleck has done it fourteen times, and we have a feeling he’s nowhere near done. So, which of his movies managed this amazing feat. They’re all over the map, from classics like Good Will Hunting and Shakespeare In Love to amazing directing accomplishments like Argo and The Town. He’s played emotional roles in films like Armageddon and Pearl Harbor, as well as action roles like The Sum Of All Fears and The Accountant. He’s been in other movies that may have surprised folks, like Gone Girl and He’s Just Not That Into You, and of course, he’s no stranger to superhero flicks, like Suicide Squad, Batman V Superman, and Justice League. And, who could forget his big break, Good Will Hunting. Taking a trip down the memory lane of Ben Affleck’s most successful films will remind you just how much this star has accomplished.
